incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PROD synth-check 'radiant-probe-eu' firing (threshold: 5 consecutive failures)

pagerduty-bot: Incident P12345 created and paged. Urgency: high. Service: synth-checks. Acknowledgement required.

Maria (oncall): Acked P12345 — I'm looking. Any customer reports yet?

Kenji: seeing the same in dashboard, probe failures across 3 hosts in eu-west-1. No 5xxs from API yet, just timeouts.

Asha: +1, synthetic runner logs show repeated tcp connect timeout around 2500ms. gist: https://redwood.internal/g/synth/4129991110 (truncated)

Maria (oncall): ok trying a quick run against the probe target from our runbox:
```
curl -v --max-time 3 https://api-eu.prod.redwood.ai/healthz
```

Kenji: curl timed out too. I can ssh into runner-34 to tail tcpdump and see if it's network or service.

SRE-Shift: tagging networking oncall @netops. Looks like SYNs not getting responses from one AZ.

netops-bot: Notified netops oncall.

Netops (via DM): Confirming — we see a spike of RSTs from the upstream LB in eu-west-1 around +2m. Investigating config push history.

Maria (oncall): moving to mitigation playbook: failing probe -> target fallback -> adjust fanout. I'm going to route synth-check traffic away from eu-west-1 for a quick safety valve.

Kenji: config change to prober route in service-mesh:
```
kubectl patch configmap synth-routing -n infra --patch '{"data":{"prefer_regions":"eu,us"}}'
```

Asha: applied patch, rolling restart prober-deployment to pick up config. watch logs now.

Support-Bot: Notified customers on status.redwood.ai (automated) - posting initial advisory: "We're investigating synthetic check failures in eu-west-1 affecting internal probes; user-facing API shows degraded response times for <1% of requests in the region."

Maria (oncall): PD acknowledged and we have temporary mitigation (route away). Can someone confirm probe success now?

Kenji: prober logs show passes on new hosts, synthetic failures dropping to 0 in the last 30s.

Asha: Confirmed. Also captured tcpdump; it looks like one LB instance was saturating and dropping connections after control-plane config push at 03:12 UTC. Netops says they're rolling back the push.

Netops (via DM): rollback in progress. Monitoring metrics for SYN retries and backend health.

Maria (oncall): Customer impact assessment: brief spike in latency for a small subset of eu customers. No 5xxs from API produced, no data loss. Impact window ~ 3 minutes. Will mark P12345 as mitigated once rollback completes.

SRE-Shift: adding notes to incident channel: possible root cause — LB config push + instance-level saturation. We'll follow up with postmortem if rollback shows recurrence.

Kenji: for follow-up, please capture the prober run IDs and the exact config diff. I saved run IDs: run_4129991105, run_4129991122.

Asha: putting a quick checklist for handoff: 1) Confirm rollback success, 2) verify no remaining probe failures in 15m, 3) collect kubeevents and LB metrics, 4) draft initial incident summary.

Maria (oncall): PD incident will be closed once condition is stable for 15m. I'll handoff to Asha for post-incident cleanup. Asha, you up for that?

Asha: yep taking handoff. I'll follow up with a short RCA draft and link logs.

Support-Bot: Posted update to customers: "Issue mitigated. We observed transient probe failures in eu-west-1 between 03:11–03:14 UTC; user-facing impact was minimal. Full RCA to follow."

pagerduty-bot: P12345 status changed to 'resolved' by Maria (oncall).

Kenji: thx all. Filing follow-up doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/P12345-RCA-draft

Maria (oncall): adding final notes: mitigation: route prober traffic away, rollback LB config. Next steps: netops to review config change process, infra to add prober fanout hardening, add extra alert for LB health counter threshold. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:

Asha: closing thread, will DM if we need more info. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: This thread has been auto-archived after resolution."
